page: The Vultr vx1-g-4c-16g-240s is a general-purpose virtual instance configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores on an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz on x86_64 architecture. The system includes 16 GB of memory, establishing a 1:4 core-to-RAM ratio, alongside 32 MB of L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and hardware-accelerated cryptographic instructions. Local storage is provided by a bundled 240 GB NVMe solid-state drive, accompanied by one complimentary public IPv4 address without discrete GPU acceleration.

Benchmark measurements indicate strong single-threaded execution, with top-tier results in single-core stress-ng tests and gzip compression reaching 39.73 GB/sec, as well as strong Geekbench text-processing output. Conversely, multi-threaded throughput demonstrates limits tied to the two physical core footprint, reflected in lower-tier results for bzip3 multi-threaded decompression and Clang software compilation. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 70.96 GB/sec, supporting steady data retrieval and maintaining 8.1 million Redis SET operations per second.

The instance delivers balanced resource efficiency for persistent enterprise services that require predictable CPU access paired with rapid local NVMe storage. Workloads aligned with this hardware profile include web application hosting, Redis caching nodes, mid-tier relational databases, and text processing microservices. It presents clear throughput tradeoffs for highly parallelized batch jobs and large model prompt processing tasks.
